statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Any sequence-invalid DCCP-Sync or DCCP-SyncAck packet MUST be ignored.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A sequence-invalid DCCP-Reset packet MUST elicit a DCCP-Sync packet in response (subject to a possible rate limit).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This response packet MUST use a new Sequence Number, and thus will increase GSS; GSR will not change, however, since the received packet was sequence-invalid.
actions: assign new Sequence Number to DCCP-Sync response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The response packet's Acknowledgement Number MUST equal GSR.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Any other sequence-invalid packet MUST elicit a similar DCCP-Sync packet, except that the response packet's Acknowledgement Number MUST equal the sequence-invalid packet's Sequence Number.
statements.pre_cond: packet.sequence_valid = false & packet.type != DCCP_Sync & packet.type != DCCP_SyncAck & packet.type != DCCP_Reset

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any other sequence-invalid packet MUST elicit a similar DCCP-Sync packet, except that the response packet's Acknowledgement Number MUST equal the sequence-invalid packet's Sequence Number.
statements.pre_cond: packet.sequence_valid = false & packet.type != DCCP_Sync & packet.type != DCCP_SyncAck & packet.type != DCCP_Reset

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: On receiving a sequence-valid DCCP-Sync packet, the peer endpoint (say, DCCP B) MUST update its GSR variable and reply with a DCCP-SyncAck packet.
statements.pre_cond: packet.sequence_valid = true & packet.type = DCCP_Sync & connection.state != REQUEST
actions: update GSR to received DCCP-Sync Sequence Number

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: As an exception, if the peer endpoint is in the REQUEST state, it MUST respond with a DCCP-Reset instead of a DCCP-SyncAck.
statements.pre_cond: connection.state = REQUEST & packet.sequence_valid = true & packet.type = DCCP_Sync

statements.subject: dccp
statements.description: To protect against denial-of-service attacks, DCCP implementations SHOULD impose a rate limit on DCCP-Syncs sent in response to sequence-invalid packets, such as not more than eight DCCP-Syncs per second.
actions: rate-limit DCCP-Sync responses to sequence-invalid packets (e.g. at most 8 per second)

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: DCCP endpoints MUST NOT process sequence-invalid packets except, perhaps, by generating a DCCP-Sync.
actions: do not process packet beyond optionally generating DCCP-Sync

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: For instance, options MUST NOT be processed.
actions: do not process options carried in sequence-invalid packet

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: An endpoint MAY temporarily preserve sequence-invalid packets in case they become valid later, however; this can reduce the impact of bursts of loss by delivering more packets to the application.
actions: optionally buffer sequence-invalid packet for potential later processing

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: In particular, an endpoint MAY preserve sequence-invalid packets for up to 2 round-trip times.
actions: buffer sequence-invalid packet for at most 2 round-trip times

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If, within that time, the relevant sequence windows change so that the packets become sequence-valid, the endpoint MAY process them again.
actions: process previously buffered packet now that it is sequence-valid

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The endpoint SHOULD use information from the original DCCP-Reset when possible.
actions: use information from original DCCP-Reset when constructing new DCCP-Reset
